bullets.title: Applying International Standards and Regulatory Requirements
bullets.text: Professional regulation differs between countries, but the underlying expectations are consistent: practise safely, maintain competence, protect the public and comply with lawful standards. An IQN must understand the local framework before practising independently.

bullets.title: Complex Consent, Capacity and Ethical Decision-Making
bullets.text: Complex decisions arise when capacity is uncertain, family views conflict, treatment burdens are high or urgent action is required. Nurses need a transparent process that separates facts, values, law and professional obligations.

bullets.title: Delegation, Advocacy and Interprofessional Accountability
bullets.text: International teams may include different nursing categories and support roles. Safe delegation requires knowledge of local scopes, patient stability and the competence of the person receiving the task. Advocacy is required when systems or decisions threaten patient rights.

bullets.title: Cultural Safety, Privacy and Professional Communication
bullets.text: International nurses care for people with diverse languages, values and experiences. Professionalism requires culturally safe communication, protection of information and awareness that power differences can affect participation.
